observations.seen: A warm key light from the upper left creates a bright falloff pool, and a lamp glow sits in the bottom-left corner. Small orange point lights mark the four power nodes. The board centre and right side go flat and murky, and the chip tops get almost no key definition.

The chip blocks and gem pedestals cast soft contact shadows onto the PCB. The shadows are mushy and low-contrast, and the chips in the maze interior lack a crisp grounding edge. The white-board variant shows the shadows best, but they are still blurry.

The faceted gems show flat per-facet shading with no environment reflection or sparkle. The chip tops have only a faint highlight. The solder mask and gold pads show no visible reflected environment, which reads like a weak or missing environment map.

The board sits on a blue cutting mat with a grid on a wooden desk, with a pegboard wall behind. The props tell a consistent maker-desk story. The surroundings are sparse and very dark, and the top band of the frame is mostly an empty brown and black wall.
Faint diagonal light shafts cross the cutting mat on the left, and a soft haze glow appears near the lamp. Nothing reads as volumetric indoor haze over the board itself.

The board colour variants (green, red, white) show solder mask, copper traces and through-holes clearly. The chips are uniform dark boxes with no package texture or legend print. The gems look like matte plastic rather than crystal.

Chips are simple bevelled cubes with tiny pins, and the gems are low-poly icosahedra on square pads. The player and enemies are small, low-detail shapes that are hard to read at this scale. The silkscreen text 'GLINT COURIER REV 4.7' is a nice touch.

The board fills about 80% of the frame, far over the 25–40% target. It is centred and symmetric with gems bracketing both sides. The playfield reads as a dense grid, and the player and enemies get lost against it.
A perspective camera at roughly 55–60° pitch shows visible keystone convergence toward the top, not an orthographic broadcast view at 70°. It is stable and readable, but the far rows compress.

Bloom shows on the player's light trail and on the power nodes. There is a soft vignette in the corners and JPEG-like softness. Frame 3 is oversaturated red with crushed blacks, and there is no clear tonemapping or colour-grade identity.

The HUD is clean and panelled, with score, hi-score, lives, shards, cache and dash bar, plus a 'Relay Grid — GO!' toast and a controls hint. A dev-style tab bar along the top takes space and clashes with the game framing. Frames 3 and 4 have no HUD.
